subject: Production latency & errors — reserved pool saturation (Silverline)
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@silverlinepayments.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@silverlinepayments.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: degraded latency + errors on reserved pool

Hi Aisha,

We started seeing elevated latency and a rising error rate on our Silverline production endpoints around 08:40 PT. Our telemetry shows token latency spiking to ~1.1s (median) and 5xxs increasing from 0.1% to ~3.7% over the last 20 minutes. This is impacting checkout flows — we've had two merchants escalate already.

We are on a reserved + dedicated pool (commit SL-3482). Your console shows our pool at 98% utilization and request queueing increasing. Can you confirm whether this is a capacity constraint on your side or something in our prompts? We already throttled a few non-critical routes and rolled a smaller model for dev traffic.

Immediate asks:
- Quick assessment: is this reserved pool saturated?
- Short-term mitigation: can you enable burst capacity or route some traffic to a hosted fallback?
- ETA on a fix/protected capacity if it's on Redwood.

We'll need an exec-level point of contact; merchant SLA impact is material and Procurement is asking about credits if SLA is missed. Attached is a screenshot from our Grafana dashboard (silverline_grafana_sla_2028-07-25.png).

Thanks — please escalate.

— Olivia
Olivia Barnes
Head of Platform Engineering, Silverline Payments
olivia@silverlinepayments.com

Folks — forwarding an urgent customer report (Silverline, deal SL-3482). Key points:

- Latency and 5xxs rising; merchant checkout impacted.
- Customer requests burst capacity or hosted fallback and asks for an exec contact re: SLA/credits.

Immediate asks:
1) Ops: confirm whether there is any hardware failure or autoscale misconfig. Provide current headroom numbers per availability zone and queue depth across pool nodes.
2) Eng (Vivek): propose a short-term mitigation (burst nodes, routing to compatible hosted variant, aggressive KV caching) and an estimate for how long it'd take to stand up burst capacity (warm-up + provisioning).
3) CS (Marissa): please join the bridge and communicate a clear customer-facing timeline.

Attachments (for ops triage): reserved_pool_topology_snapshot.json, silverline_grafana_sla_2028-07-25.png, temporary_burst_quote_SLV-3482.pdf

I've started a bridge (Zoom link in calendar) — can someone confirm they've joined? I'll loop in Execs if we can't clear within 2 hours.

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.ai, operations@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production: degraded latency + errors on reserved pool (Silverline)

Joining the bridge now. Quick triage:
- No node hardware alerts in the last 24h; autoscaler logged normal activity but noted an "allocation delay" spike for AZ-us-west-2a between 08:35-08:50.
- Pool-level queue depth shows sustained backpressure on two GPU nodes that are running long KV-cache-heavy sessions (customer workload with long context windows).

Short-term mitigations I'm ordering now (ETA ~8-12 minutes):
- Provision 4 warm burst instances from the burst pool and attach them to the reserved pool. Warm-up ~6 minutes; provisioning + routing ~8-12 minutes.
- Apply per-route aggressive prefix/KV cache eviction for non-critical routes to free memory on saturated nodes.
- Route up to 20% of traffic for non-critical endpoints to the compatible hosted model variant in us-east-1 (lower-memory quantized variant) to relieve the queue.

If burst attaches successfully, expected median token latency should drop below 450ms within 15 minutes. I'm pushing higher-priority scheduling for Silverline since this is a high-impact merchant.

I'm also flagging this as a reserved-throughput shortfall: their commit was sized based on typical 16k context workloads; current mixture of sustained 64k-like sessions plus KV-heavy ops exceeds provisioned throughput. We need an ops follow-up to analyze whether our autoscaler should consider session-length signals for faster scaling.

Will update on the bridge.
— Vivek

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@silverlinepayments.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Jul 2028 15:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: degraded latency + errors on reserved pool (Silverline)

Olivia — thanks for the heads-up and patience. Quick summary of where we landed and next steps for Silverline: 

What we did (short term):
- Attached 4 warm burst GPUs; observed queue depths return to normal within ~12 minutes. Median token latency dropped to ~380ms and 5xxs subsided to ~0.2%.
- Routed 18% of non-checkout traffic to our hosted compatible variant while we evaluate sustained load.
- Applied aggressive KV eviction to free headroom on long-lived sessions.

What we found:
- The reserved pool was effectively saturated because a few long-context sessions (64k-like) persisted longer than our sizing assumptions for SL-3482. These sessions caused per-node KV memory pressure and prevented efficient autoscale rebalancing.

Next / action items:
- Ops will produce a post-incident snapshot (reserved_pool_topology_snapshot.json) and run a headroom analysis across AZs (due EOD PT).
- Eng (Vivek) and Product will assess an autoscaler improvement: incorporate session-length signals and pre-warm policies for committed pools (ETA: design doc by 2028-08-02).
- Sales/Customer success: we'll open a compensation dialog if SLA thresholds were breached; Client Finance and Procurement are looped via HS-Record-592174.

Temporary offer: we provided a 7-day temporary burst credit (see temporary_burst_quote_SLV-3482.pdf) while we work through a long-term sizing and autoscale fix.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up sync with your platform leads tomorrow to walk through telemetry and longer-term sizing recommendations. Please let me know a preferred time.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
